title: Quantum Hashing Circuit Optimization for Arbitrary Qubit Connectivity Graphs Based on 1-Covering Path
authors: Kamil Khadiev, Aliya Khadieva, Vadim Sagitov, Kamil Khasanov, Mansur Ziatdinov
abstract: One of the obstacles to the widespread adoption of quantum computing is the problem of efficient circuit synthesis. Current quantum hardware has limited connections between qubits, with each qubit connected to only a few others. This means that the circuit has to be transformed to accommodate this. In this paper, we present an algorithm that converts a circuit containing a sequence of CNOT gates into a form that is suitable for arbitrary quantum computer architectures. Although we demonstrate the algorithm only in the context of quantum fingerprinting, similar gate sequences are prevalent in quantum algorithms; for instance, they are present in the textbook quantum Fourier transform. We present a quantum circuit implementation of the quantum hashing algorithm (quantum fingerprinting algorithm) for a quantum device with restrictions on the application of two-qubit gates that are expressed as a qubit connectivity graph. As an example of usage of the technique, we apply it to quantum finite automata recognizing the unary $MOD_p=\{a^\ell: \ell \bmod p=0\}$ language, and the $EQ_p=\{a^\ell b^r: \ell \equiv r \pmod p\}$ language. Given the enhancements that our algorithm provides~-- for instance, in one case it achieves a 16\%--17\% decrease in CNOT circuit cost~-- we believe it could also be useful in a broader quantum compilation context.
summary: This paper develops an algorithm to efficiently synthesize quantum circuits for quantum hashing when the underlying quantum hardware has limited qubit connectivity. It achieves this by mapping the required gate sequence onto a path found in the graph representing qubit connections, significantly reducing the necessary CNOT gate count. This work provides a general framework for optimizing quantum algorithms for realistic, constrained quantum devices.
main_problem: The core problem is efficiently synthesizing quantum circuits, specifically for quantum hashing (fingerprinting), to run on hardware with limited qubit connectivity.
main_result: The authors present an algorithm that converts CNOT gate sequences into a form suitable for arbitrary architectures by solving the Shortest Non-simple 1-covering Path Problem (1-SNSCPP).
method: The method relies on finding a shortest 1-covering path in the qubit connectivity graph and constructing quantum gates using control rotations (CR) and SWAP gates to simulate the required transformations along this path.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum circuit operating on qubits constrained by an arbitrary, fixed qubit connectivity graph G=(V, E). The algorithm applies to quantum hashing circuits used for tasks like recognizing specific formal languages.
key_observables: CNOT cost (the primary metric of efficiency), and the probability of accepting a string in the quantum fingerprinting scheme.
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n$), the length of the input word ($\ell$), and the structure of the connectivity graph $G$.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes the availability of a solution for the 1-SNSCPP problem, which is NP-hard; approximations are used to manage this complexity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the shallow circuit structure for quantum fingerprinting and show how complex gates like $CR_y$ and $SWAP$ can be decomposed into basic CNOT and rotation gates.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the graph theory component (solving 1-SNSCPP), derives the gate decomposition costs based on path properties ($k$, $k'$), and finally presents the overall CNOT cost formula for $\ell$ applications of the hashing operator.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum computation, the reliance on graph algorithms (like finding covering paths) to optimize physical implementation constraints is a general theme relevant to designing complex quantum hardware protocols.
